title: No Relief Yet For Thai Stock Market

organizations.name: thai stock market no relief yet for thai stock market

text:
No Relief Yet For Thai Stock Market 29: The Thai stock market has moved lower in back-to-back trading days, sliding more than 25 points or 1.6 percent along the way. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now rests just beneath the 1,655-point plateau and it's looking at another soft start again on Tuesday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is soft, with weakness expected among the technology stocks and oil companies. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourse are expected to follow suit.
The SET finished modestly lower on Monday following losses from the financial shares and the energy producers.
For the day, the index shed 13.67 points or 0.82 percent to finish at 1,654.85 after trading between 1,654.80 and 1,673.42. Volume was 10.121 billion shares worth 28.826 billion baht. There were 1,167 decliners and 286 gainers, with 328 stocks finishing unchanged.
Among the actives, Advanced Info eased 0.27 percent, while Thailand Airport shed 0.38 percent, Banpu tumbled 2.23 percent, Bangkok Bank lost 0.93 percent, Bangkok Medical fell 0.81 percent, Beauty Community plunged 3.52 percent, Bangkok Expressway retreated 2.30 percent, Charoen Pokphand Foods climbed 1.00 percent, Kasikornbank contracted 2.90 percent, Krung Thai Bank dipped 0.49 percent, PTT Global Chemical was down 0.32 percent, Siam Commercial Bank skidded 1.08 percent, Siam Concrete gave away 1.39 percent and PTT and PTT Exploration and Production were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is broadly negative as stocks moved sharply lower on Monday, extending losses from the previous session.
The Dow plunged 602.12 points or 2.32 percent to 25,387.18, while the NASDAQ dropped 206.03 points or 2.78 percent to 7,200.87 and the S&P fell 54.79 points or 1.97 percent to 2,726.22.
A sharp decline by shares of Apple ( AAPL ) and General Electric (GE) weighed on the markets, while concerns about the outlook for global economic growth and a continued increase in interest rates also contributed to the sell-off.
Light trading activity may have exaggerated the downward move, however, as government offices, the bond markets, and most banks were closed in observance of Veterans Day.
Crude oil shook off early gains on Monday to end lower for the 11th straight session on oversupply concerns. Crude oil futures for December, which rose to $61.28 earlier in the session, settled lower by $0.26 or 0.4 percent at $59.93 a barrel, the lowest settlement since February. //www.rttnews.com/2954369/no-relief-yet-for-thai-stock-market.aspx
